participants: Beth Martin (claimant; daughter of deceased member Alan Martin)
summary: Beth Martin and Alicia Romero discussed request REQ-2025-11-01 and complaint C-e1da28538652e263887a. Beth said she has sent the same documents three times and, in frustrated terms, said she does not understand what else is wanted. She said she recalls being told the papers were all accepted, distinguished uploading documents from a formal benefit decision, and asked Alicia to identify exactly which item is missing. Alicia confirmed she holds Beth's email from this morning with four attachments, including the portal upload receipt, which shows DC-11, ID-11 and RF-11 as received. She said she had not yet had a reply from the specialist team, so could not say whether DC-11 had been assessed or what is outstanding, and gave no assurance that everything is complete. Alicia said she will ask Alice Hughes (Death Benefits Administration) for the case-specific records; she gave no date. Beth agreed to that step but said the matter is not sorted and she is not happy.
follow_up_items: Alicia Romero to request case-specific records from Alice Hughes, Death Benefits Administration. No due date stated.

conversation.speaker: Alicia Romero
conversation.text: Good morning Beth, it's Alicia Romero from the complaints team. Thanks for picking up.

conversation.speaker: Beth Martin
conversation.text: Hello. I've just sent you another email, I don't know if you've seen it yet.

conversation.speaker: Alicia Romero
conversation.text: I have, it came in this morning with the four attachments. Before anything else, I'm sorry about your father. I know this is a hard time to be chasing paperwork.

conversation.speaker: Beth Martin
conversation.text: Thank you. It's just that I keep being asked for the same things. I've sent the documents three times now. I don't understand what else you want from me.

conversation.speaker: Alicia Romero
conversation.text: I hear you. Let me check I've got the concern right. The request is REQ-2025-11-01. The death certificate, DC-11, has been asked for again even though you uploaded it in December, and you want to know exactly which item is missing.

conversation.speaker: Beth Martin
conversation.text: Yes. And I was told the papers were all accepted. I know that's not the same as the benefit being decided, that's a separate thing. But I was told they were all accepted, and now this.

conversation.speaker: Alicia Romero
conversation.text: I'm not doubting that that's what you recall. I can't tell you what was said before the complaint, though, and I don't want to confirm it either way until I've seen the records. What I can tell you is what I actually have in front of me, which is

conversation.text: So you can't tell me what's missing.

conversation.speaker: Alicia Romero
conversation.text: Not yet. What I have is your request reference, the three documents and the upload receipt image. The receipt shows DC-11, ID-11 and RF-11 as received on the portal. A receipt tells me the files arrived. It doesn't tell me on its own whether DC-11 has been assessed against the requirement, and I haven't had a reply from the specialist team yet. I'd rather say that than tell you everything is fine and turn out to be wrong.

conversation.speaker: Beth Martin
conversation.text: That's what I was told last time. That it was all fine.

conversation.speaker: Alicia Romero
conversation.text: I understand why that's frustrating. What I can do is ask Alice Hughes in Death Benefits Administration for the case-specific records: what was recorded when DC-11 came in, and what the checklist shows now. Then I'll know what to tell you.

conversation.speaker: Beth Martin
conversation.text: And when will I hear back?

conversation.speaker: Alicia Romero
conversation.text: I can't give you a date I can't stand behind, Beth, because it depends on what the specialist team can find. I'd rather be straight with you about that.

conversation.speaker: Beth Martin
conversation.text: Right. I'll be honest, I'm not happy. It's the third time I've sent them.

conversation.speaker: Alicia Romero
conversation.text: That's fair, and I've got it down that you sent them with your first email, with the complaint, and again this morning.

conversation.speaker: Beth Martin
conversation.text: Fine. Ask her. But as far as I'm concerned it isn't sorted.

conversation.speaker: Alicia Romero
conversation.text: Understood. Thank you for your patience, Beth.
